blueprint_topic: Management of Care — individualized stroke discharge and transition planning
stem: A client hospitalized with acute ischemic stroke is preparing for transition to postacute care. Which action by the RN best reflects current stroke-discharge guidance?

options.A: Begin and update discharge planning during hospitalization with the client and family, using rehabilitation needs and medication and recurrent-stroke education to shape the transition.
options.B: Select the postacute setting from the client's current motor status, then address medication education and family preparation after placement is finalized.
options.C: Delay detailed transition planning until the discharge date is known so changing neurologic deficits do not require repeated revision of the plan.
options.D: Use the standard stroke discharge pathway to determine placement first, then individualize rehabilitation and family needs after the client reaches postacute care.

rationale: A is correct. The 2026 American Heart Association scientific statement on nursing stroke care states that discharge planning should begin early and remain dynamic, guided by patient and family needs assessments. It also identifies predischarge rehabilitation assessment as important for determining the appropriate postacute setting and services and emphasizes nursing education about lifestyle changes, medication adherence, and recognition of recurrent-stroke symptoms. The 2026 AHA/ASA acute ischemic stroke guideline separately supports multidisciplinary inpatient rehabilitation evaluation to determine the appropriate rehabilitation level. B is incorrect because it narrows placement planning mainly to motor status and postpones other transition needs rather than using an individualized multidomain assessment. C is incorrect because current guidance supports early, evolving planning rather than waiting until the discharge date is fixed. D is incorrect because standardized pathways can support care, but patient/family and rehabilitation needs should guide the transition before discharge rather than being individualized only after postacute placement.
educational_objective: Begin stroke discharge planning early and revise it as needs evolve, using patient/family assessment, predischarge rehabilitation needs, and medication and recurrent-stroke education to support an individualized transition.
source_organization: American Heart Association; American Heart Association/American Stroke Association
source_document_title: Targeted Nursing Interventions for Improving Stroke Care and Outcomes in the Rural Setting; 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke

source_locator: 2026 AHA scientific statement — Posthyperacute and Discharge: nurses educate patients about lifestyle changes, medication adherence, and recognition of recurrent-stroke symptoms; discharge planning should begin early and remain dynamic, guided by patient and family needs assessments; predischarge rehabilitation assessments are important for determining the appropriate postacute stroke setting and services. 2026 AHA/ASA AIS guideline — Section 5.7 Rehabilitation, Synopsis and Recommendation-Specific Supportive Text 1: multidisciplinary inpatient rehabilitation evaluation helps determine the appropriate rehabilitation intensity/modality and level of care.
source_claim_supported: Stroke discharge planning should begin early, remain dynamic and individualized to patient/family needs, incorporate predischarge rehabilitation assessment for postacute setting/services, and include nursing education about medication adherence and recurrent-stroke symptom recognition.

correction_summary: Rebuilt an extremely cueable all-in-one discharge-plan answer into a balanced RN transition-planning item. Removed the 'only' distractor and extreme answer-length cue, retained the early/dynamic individualized planning construct, and limited the key to directly supported discharge-planning elements. Adversarial reread removed a broader follow-up-planning phrase that was not as directly supported by the primary 2026 locator.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly reflects early/dynamic patient-family-centered planning, predischarge rehabilitation assessment, and medication/recurrent-stroke education.
option_audit.B: Plausible motor-dominant sequencing error; incorrect because discharge planning should integrate multidomain patient/family needs rather than defer them until placement is finalized.
option_audit.C: Plausible wait-for-stability error; incorrect because guidance explicitly supports beginning discharge planning early and updating it dynamically.
option_audit.D: Plausible standardized-pathway error; incorrect because standardized processes do not replace individualized patient/family and rehabilitation planning before transition.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on always/never/only/all/must-type absolutes.
cueing_audit.answer_length: All four options contain comparable transition-planning detail; the key is not uniquely signaled by length.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four options are parallel RN discharge-planning actions within the same construct.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified after AHA/AHA-ASA source-based reread.
